summary: Guidance for safe backstop and feature sunsetting of optimizer flags without snapshot restore
description: Issue summary: Customer Lumina Health plans to sunset an experimental optimizer flag (async-prefix-prefetch) across several tenant pools but does not have snapshot backups for the feature-state. They requested a backstop strategy that does not rely on snapshot restore to ensure safe rollback and no customer-visible regression. Impact: potential 95p/99p latency increase and token cost changes during sunsetting; possible transient 5xx for tenants with mixed-optimizer-profiles. Environment: Dedicated GPU pool (prod, us-east) serving gpt-3.5-redwood-v2 and gpt-4-lite. Steps to reproduce/context: 1) Toggle optimizer flag off via console feature toggle for a small subset of tenants. 2) Observe latency and error metrics for the next 15 minutes. 3) Gradually expand toggle to remaining tenants. Observed behavior: Customers report small but sustained 95p latency increase (200-350ms) and occasional 524 timeouts for long-streaming sessions after flag removal. Expected behavior: Controlled change with minimal latency regression; ability to return to pre-change behavior quickly without snapshot restore. Logs & telemetry pointers: linked APM traces in Datadog (service:redwood-serving, trace-ids included in investigation notes), console audit logs for toggle operations, metric dashboards at https://console.redwood/dash/ops/optimizer-sunset.
investigation_notes: Hypotheses: 1) Removing async-prefix-prefetch disables aggressive KV prefetching, increasing per-request token computation and causing tail latency spikes for long-sequence streaming. 2) Mixed tenant routing causes some requests to land on nodes with warmed KV cache and others on cold nodes, amplifying variance. 3) Autoscaler reaction lag for certain worker types can increase queueing when traffic pattern shifts. Findings so far: - Correlated tail latency spikes to nodes that lost both prefetch and had recent model cold-starts (see trace cluster IDs). - No evidence of model binary change or kernel regression; CPU/GPU utilization increases modestly. - Rolling disable in small cohort shows transient spikes lasting ~10-20 minutes per pool. Temporary mitigations applied: enabled traffic-splitting to keep 10% traffic on optimized variant, throttled background batch jobs, increased per-worker concurrency limit to reduce queueing. Next hypotheses to validate: test controlled drain + staggered worker recycle to allow KV warmup without snapshot restore.

resolution: Planned backstop strategy (not yet executed): 1) Pre-create traffic-split routes and guard rails in Console for tenant pools; 2) Run a Canary sequence: start at 5% optimized-disabled, monitor 95p/99p latency, error-rate, kv-cache-hit. Hold for 30 minutes at each step. 3) If 95p delta > 150ms or errors > 0.5%, immediately revert traffic-split to 100% optimized variant; 4) Use staggered worker drain (5min between hosts) for warmup instead of snapshot restore. Follow-ups: - Create a one-click Console backstop button for future sunsetting (task created for product team). - Add automated hold points into the Console Canary workflow (linked feature request: ENG-FT-2301). - Draft post-window telemetry checklist for Lumina Health. Owners: Diego (SRE) and Maya (Support). Expected rollback time SLA: <= 15 minutes to fully re-route traffic back to optimized variant.
